label: 论据
text: Iterative Magnitude Pruning applied to mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks trained on the CIFAR10 image classification dataset produces sparse subnetworks that match or in some cases surpass the dense unpruned Bayesian model's test accuracy across multiple architectures for a wide sparsity range , with performance degradation appearing only in very high sparsity regimes
完整表述: Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) applied to mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) trained on the CIFAR10 image classification dataset produces sparse subnetworks (mask-plus-original-initialization pairs) that match or in some cases surpass the dense unpruned Bayesian model's test accuracy across multiple architectures for a wide sparsity range, with performance degradation appearing only in very high sparsity regimes.

label: 论据
text: (matching performance observed up to roughly 90% sparsity)

label: assertion
text: Bayesian variants of the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis hold empirically for the evaluated models and dataset.
完整表述: Bayesian variants of the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis hold empirically for the evaluated mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks and the CIFAR10 image classification dataset.

label: assertion
text: pruning based primarily on the absolute posterior mean yields competitive ticket performance
完整表述: In Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) pruned under Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP), pruning based primarily on the absolute posterior mean ($s_{mm}=|\mu|$, mu-magnitude) yields competitive ticket performance.

label: assertion
text: , with the signal-to-noise ratio score performing similarly
完整表述: In Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) pruned under Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP), the signal-to-noise ratio score ($s_{SNR}=|\mu|/\sigma$) performs similarly to pruning based primarily on the absolute posterior mean.

label: assertion
text: the squared-sum score yields substantially worse results
完整表述: In Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) pruned under Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP), the squared-sum score ($s_{ss}=\sqrt{\mu^2+\sigma^2}$) yields substantially worse results than pruning based primarily on the absolute posterior mean and the signal-to-noise ratio score ($s_{SNR}=|\mu|/\sigma$), notably on the Vision Transformer ViT-tiny model.

label: assertion
text: , causing earlier performance degradation at increasing sparsity.
完整表述: In Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) pruned under Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP), the squared-sum score ($s_{ss}=\sqrt{\mu^2+\sigma^2}$) causes performance degradation at increasing sparsity earlier than pruning based primarily on the absolute posterior mean and the signal-to-noise ratio score ($s_{SNR}=|\mu|/\sigma$).

label: assertion
text: pruning decisions for mean-field variational BNNs should rely primarily on the posterior mean magnitude and only secondarily on posterior standard deviation.
完整表述: Pruning decisions for mean-field variational BNNs should rely primarily on the posterior mean magnitude and only secondarily on posterior standard deviation.
